Class EquinixRateCard

java.lang.Object
com.eqixiac.equinix.design.value.ratecard.EquinixRateCard
All Implemented Interfaces:
RateCard
public final class EquinixRateCard extends Object implements RateCard
A RateCard backed by the live Equinix Fabric Pricing API (fabric.prices()); the authoritative source of Equinix-side connection and Cloud Router prices for the cost, savings, and TCO models.

The fetch is narrowed server-side by price /type to the two product families this card prices — virtual connections (PriceType.VIRTUAL_CONNECTION_PRODUCT) and Cloud Routers (PriceType.CLOUD_ROUTER_PRODUCT) — rather than pulling the whole catalogue (ports, IP blocks, …) and discarding most of it. A connection price row still carries its connection type and metro only in its code/name (the structured descriptor holds just the bandwidth), so the card matches those remaining axes client-side over the (much smaller) cached set. The metro is matched against a whole delimited token of the code/name, never a bare two-letter substring, so a metro code like AT/DE cannot false-match an unrelated word. Cloud Router rows carry a structured descriptor and are matched on it: exact package-code equality plus the row's own metroCode.

Both lookups honour the request's remaining axes strictly. When a metro is requested, a row of another metro is never returned — the lookup yields empty instead, so a layered card can consult a lower layer that may hold a genuine figure for that metro. The live catalogue is also term-scoped, so rows whose termLength matches the requested Term are preferred; when only a different-term row exists, it is returned with a note naming the substitution (never silently), and a row without a termLength is term-neutral.

The card is fault-tolerant: if the catalogue cannot be fetched (network error, unauthenticated client, endpoint unavailable), it yields Optional.empty() for every lookup so callers fall back to another rate card or a heuristic rather than failing, and it reports the failure through isLiveSourceUnavailable(). Every quote it does produce is tagged PriceSource.EQUINIX_LIVE.

Each type-scoped query is paged in full and the combined result cached for the card's lifetime once a fetch fully succeeds. A fetch in which any type-scoped query failed is not cached and is retried on the next lookup, so a transient 429/5xx/auth error never permanently poisons the card. A lookup that finds no matching or no priced row simply defers to the fallback — never a wrong or phantom-zero number.

    • connection

      public Optional<PriceQuote> connection(ConnectionType type, int bandwidthMbps, MetroCode metro, Term term)
      Description copied from interface: RateCard
      Resolves the price of a single Fabric connection / virtual connection.

      Implementation contract. The matching strategy is implementation-specific, and a card whose data lacks an axis (metro, term, type) still returns its best figure — or empty — rather than failing; callers must not assume every card is sensitive to every parameter. Of the bundled cards: CustomRateCard resolves the most specific declared entry (exact metro+term down to metro/term-agnostic, then a declared default); EquinixRateCard matches bandwidth and type against the live catalogue, honours a requested metro strictly (a wrong-metro row is never returned), and prefers a term-matched row — a different-term row is only ever returned with a note naming the substitution; ReferenceRateCard matches on bandwidth alone (smallest tabulated tier at or above the request, linearly extrapolated with an EXTRAPOLATED note above the top tier) and ignores type, metro, and term entirely.

      Specified by:
      connection in interface RateCard
      Parameters:
      type - the connection type (e.g. EVPL_VC); may be null for any type
      bandwidthMbps - the provisioned bandwidth in Mbps
      metro - the metro the connection originates in (may be null if metro-agnostic)
      term - the commitment term (may be null if term-agnostic)
      Returns:
      the resolved quote, or Optional.empty() if this card cannot price the connection

    • cloudRouter

      public Optional<PriceQuote> cloudRouter(String packageCode, MetroCode metro, Term term)
      Description copied from interface: RateCard
      Resolves the price of a single Fabric Cloud Router instance.

      Implementation contract. As with RateCard.connection(ConnectionType, int, MetroCode, Term), matching is implementation-specific and cards without a metro/term axis return their best figure regardless. Of the bundled cards: CustomRateCard resolves the most specific declared (packageCode, metro, term) entry; EquinixRateCard matches the package code and metro structurally against the row's own descriptor (exact package equality, the row's own metro code) and prefers a term-matched row, labelling any term substitution; ReferenceRateCard ignores metro and term, and substitutes its STANDARD figure for an unlisted package with a note naming the substitution.

      Specified by:
      cloudRouter in interface RateCard
      Parameters:
      packageCode - the router package / tier code (e.g. "STANDARD"); may be null for any
      metro - the metro the router is deployed in (may be null if metro-agnostic)
      term - the commitment term (may be null if term-agnostic)
      Returns:
      the resolved quote, or Optional.empty() if this card cannot price the router

    • isLiveSourceUnavailable

      public boolean isLiveSourceUnavailable()
      Whether the most recent attempt to fetch the live price catalogue failed (network error, unauthenticated client, 429/5xx). When true, an empty lookup result means "the live source could not be reached", not "no such price"; the next lookup retries the fetch. A successful fetch — even one that legitimately returns no rows — clears this. Lets callers distinguish an empty catalogue from a failed fetch.
      Returns:
      true if the last catalogue fetch failed and rows may be missing
